title: ASIC warning receives wide support
full_text:
The SMSF Association has renewed its support for a ban on harmful lead generation practices following the release yesterday of the Australian Securities and Investments Commission’s (ASIC) report into the practice.
“We support a ban on high-risk lead generation that exposes consumers to harm. Reforms must address the conduct and commercial incentives driving that harm, while preserving legitimate professional referrals, education and access to financial advice,” association chief executive Peter Burgess said.
Burgess pointed out the regulator’s review focused on licensees that had identified links to lead generation and were not representative of the broader financial advice profession.
“ASIC’s findings should now guide where stronger safeguards are needed and where existing obligations need to be enforced,” he suggested.
The Association of Superannuation Funds of Australia (ASFA) also welcomed the corporate watchdog’s firm stance on the issue.
“ASIC’s position is clear. However, enforcement action often comes after people have already lost money,” ASFA chief executive Mary Delahunty said.
According to the superannuation industry peak body, the warning from ASIC effectively bans lead generators from the advice process, a measure it backs.
“As the government develops the consumer protection reforms [Financial Services Minister] Dr [Daniel] Mulino announced in August, ASFA is calling for legislation that bans lead generators from the advice process outright so Australians are protected before any money is lost,” Delahunty indicated.
The Super Members Council (SMC) is likewise calling for an outright ban as the “only credible policy answer to protect Australians’ life savings”.
“Even after the Shield and First Guardian collapses, ASIC’s report methodically catalogues the types of shocking consumer harm being caused by lead generators working for some licensed entities,” SMC chief executive Misha Schubert said, adding the regulator’s report should be ringing alarm bells in Canberra.
The ASIC report, “Lead generation advice models: Putting consumers and licensees at risk”, reviewed 15 organisations with an Australian financial services licence and their representatives identified as having links to lead generation activities.
author: Jason Spits
